name: Pepper Leaf Spot (Cercospora)
description: A fungal disease causing circular spots on pepper leaves. It reduces photosynthetic capacity and can cause significant defoliation during wet seasons, impacting fruit yield and quality.
symptoms: Circular to irregular tan or gray spots with dark borders
Spots on older leaves first, progressing upward
Spots coalescing causing large necrotic areas
causes: Extended leaf wetness from rain or irrigation
Dense plantings with poor air circulation
Fungal survival on infected crop debris
treatments: Apply copper-based fungicides at first symptoms
Spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil at 7-10 day intervals
Remove and destroy infected lower leaves
prevention: Space plants adequately for air circulation
Use drip irrigation to keep foliage dry
Mulch around plants to reduce soil splash
Practice crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops
